Hashemi Rafsanjani et al. arXiv:1208.2706 Eq. (5)

Independent bounded log-gamma root and endpoint check with m=floor(n^(1/3)): endpoint fractions about 0.004633, 5.61e-7 and 6.209e-11 at n=100,1000,5000. The analytic endpoint bound is uniform on positive logarithmic brackets, unlike these sample values.
correctness.rationale: A rate-r full replacement makes the state independent of the initialization after the first reset. Its stationary renewal mixture has Q=exp(-gamma t) with density a q^(a-1). A word of weight b receives the beta-integral population p_b, and the only coherence is c=E[Q^(n/2)]/2=a/(n+2a). The X-state concurrence formula counts each complementary pair once; cancellation of common gamma factors then gives exactly R_n. The derivative of each positive summand divided by that summand is 2/(n+2a) minus half the two reciprocal sums with n+2 terms in total. Their lower bound (n+2)/(2(a+n)) suffices, strictly. The endpoint b=1,n-1 alone gives R_n(0+)>1 for n>=3, while R_n tends to zero at large a; at n=2, R_2=1/(a+2). For a in any fixed positive logarithmic bracket, cut off m=floor(n^(1/3)) terms at either end. The log gamma ratio g(b)=log Gamma(b+a)-log Gamma(b+1) is concave for a>1 by monotonicity of trigamma, so the complementary summand rises toward the center; the tails are bounded by 2m times the summand at m, exponentially negligible in (log n)^2 relative to the central term by the gamma-ratio estimate at m and n/2. In the interior the relative error O(a^2/m) vanishes. The beta-integrand Riemann sum has relative error O(sqrt(a)/n) by unimodality and its peak-to-integral ratio, and the truncated beta tails vanish relatively. Applying the duplication formula or Stirling gives R_n=(n/4)2^(-a)sqrt(2 pi/a)(1+o(1)) uniformly there. Bracketing the unique root first gives a_n/log n -> 1/log 2; substituting in the log of the root equation gives the stated constant and negative half-log-log correction.
residual_risks: The asymptotic formula is not a certified finite-n error estimate. The conclusion is for zero-temperature independent damping and full entangled GHZ re-preparation; it is not stationarity of a reset-conditioned pure state or an LOCC protocol.

evidence: The X-state theorem applies exactly to the stationary matrix but does not specify its entries or the large-size threshold. Wald et al. use discrete unitary steps, with renewal weights depending on the reset rule. The examined recent reset-entanglement work studies Ising unitary steps and averaged versus resolved entropy and two-qubit concurrence; the hardware study uses noisy mid-circuit measurement and conditional resets.
broader_coverage.reasoning: There is no implication from unitary-step resonance or conditional measurement/reset models to orientation-dependent amplitude damping and the beta-function population sum of a common GHZ replacement clock.

value.rationale: The stationary boundary gives the quantitative cost, in reset rate versus spontaneous-emission rate, for maintaining genuine multipartite entanglement. It distinguishes a logarithmic cost with a controlled correction from the linear cost found for depolarization under the same preparation protocol. The strict monotonicity and all-size criterion make that distinction directly usable in the idealized model.
residual_risks: Re-preparation itself supplies entanglement; the result is not a claim about generating entanglement locally, imperfect reset fidelity or finite-temperature noise.
